solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Animals no end of a nuisance (4)

indicators.note: a thing with no end has lost its last part, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: the article taken as it stands
a pest is a nuisance, here minus its last letter T

annotation.surface: Someone complaining that animals are an endless nuisance.
annotation.walkthrough: "No end of a nuisance" reads as a grumble about how troublesome the animals are, but it tells you to cut the tail off A PEST.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: apes, like gorillas and chimps, are one kind of animal.

entries.clue: Against, say, pressure connected with job (11)

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
re means concerning, connected with
a job is a position

annotation.surface: Someone objecting to the pressure that comes with their job.
annotation.walkthrough: "Against" looks like an attitude of opposition, but the clue treats it as a word, and "say" warns that it is only an example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: grammatically, against is a word of the class that includes on, with and under.

entries.clue: Dropping off three characters in succession in channel (9)

indicators.note: what is in a channel lies within it, so the letters go inside the channel's name

blocks.note: the Solent, the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, split to hold the rest
three letters that follow one another in the alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone nodding off while three characters parade across a TV channel.
annotation.walkthrough: The channel sounds like television, but it is a stretch of sea off southern England, and the characters are letters of the alphabet, not people on screen.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: somnolent means drowsy, on the point of dropping off to sleep.

entries.clue: Dropping in Nana, Barrie’s first dog, for surgery (10)

indicators.note: a name's first is its opening letter
something sent for surgery gets cut up and put back together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the first letter of Barrie
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Nana, the dog in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan, dropping in at the vet's for an operation.
annotation.walkthrough: Nana is the Newfoundland nursemaid in Barrie's Peter Pan, so the surface hangs together; "Dropping in" looks like a visit, but only "Dropping" is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dropping a plan or a friend means giving it up, deserting it.

entries.clue: Comes down as dawn breaks (7)

indicators.note: one thing that breaks another splits it open, so the dawn goes into the middle of AS

blocks.note: the word taken as it stands, split to hold the rest
dawn is first light

annotation.surface: Something descending just as day breaks.
annotation.walkthrough: "Dawn breaks" is a stock phrase, which hides that dawn is a piece and "breaks" an instruction to put it inside the little word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bird or a passenger alights, coming down to settle or get off.

entries.clue: Anglicans hire me to translate this speech (8,7)

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: English churchgoers hiring an interpreter for a speech in a foreign tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is that Anglicans, the very English church, should need a translator for the American version of their own language.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by self-reference: the speech the Anglicans want translated is the one their letters make, the variety spoken in the USA.

entries.clue: Strip of French ground around Left Bank in Paris (7)

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it, so the ground wraps round the letter
the left bank of a written word is its left-hand edge, the first letter

blocks.note: de is French for of
ground is soil, split to hold the rest
the leftmost letter of Paris

annotation.surface: Stripping French ground near the Left Bank, the artists' quarter south of the Seine in Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: The Left Bank of Paris is a real district, which is why nobody reads it as the left edge of the word Paris.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to despoil a place is to plunder it, strip it of its valuables.

entries.clue: Somewhat cylindrical little creature (5)

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only some of the next word is used

blocks.note: the middle of the word, with cyl- and -cal trimmed off

annotation.surface: A small animal with a roughly tube-shaped body.
annotation.walkthrough: The indri is a lemur from Madagascar, the largest living one, so "little" is generous.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the indri is a lemur, one kind of creature.

entries.clue: Diver trapped by icebergs moving northwards (5)

indicators.note: something trapped by a word is held inside it
in a down clue, moving north means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: the inside of the word, with ic- and -s trimmed off

annotation.surface: A diver caught between icebergs drifting towards the pole.
annotation.walkthrough: The diver is a bird, not a person in a wetsuit, which the icy surface makes easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the grebe is a waterbird that dives for its food.

entries.clue: Appears to admit verses’ decency (10)

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them in, so the verses go inside

blocks.note: appears = seems, split to hold the rest
verses are lines of poetry

annotation.surface: Poems that look respectable on the surface.
annotation.walkthrough: COMELINESS fits the same letters at the end and tempts first, but no word for appears can hold it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: seemliness is propriety, behaviour that is decent and fitting.

entries.clue: Border in London Fields? (4)

blocks.note: the straight meaning: a boundary or rim
the surface wants a place name; the setter means the border of a field as a Cockney would say it

annotation.surface: A boundary in London Fields, a park in Hackney, east London.
annotation.walkthrough: London Fields is a real park, which hides the joke: a Londoner's field border is a 'edge. The question mark flags the dialect pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An edge is a border, and in a Cockney accent the hedge round a field comes out as the same word.

entries.clue: Beside the water, a second lizard (6)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, as in "wait a mo"
a loch is a Scottish lake

annotation.surface: A lizard basking by a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: "A second" gives MO as a whole, not A plus S, which throws solvers who don't know the lizard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the moloch, or thorny devil, is a spiky Australian lizard.

entries.clue: Puritan clubs fish (8)

blocks.note: irons are golf clubs
the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A Puritan attacking fish with clubs.
annotation.walkthrough: The clubs are golf clubs, not a card suit or cudgels.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: the Ironsides were Cromwell's Puritan cavalry in the English Civil War, and each trooper was an Ironside.

entries.clue: Part of digestive system is in fact now free of foreign bodies (11)

indicators.note: what is in something lies inside it, so the gut and IS sit within the word for fact

blocks.note: "in deed" and "in fact" are the same; split to hold the rest
the colon is part of the gut
the word taken as it stands

annotation.surface: A medical report that the gut is finally clear of foreign bodies.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical picture hides a political definition: the foreign bodies are colonial powers, not objects swallowed.
annotation.definitionFit: A political sense: a decolonised country has shed its foreign rulers, the bodies of the clue.

entries.clue: Ready to tear back from office (4)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so take the last letter

blocks.note: to tear is to rip
the last letter of office

annotation.surface: Someone eager to rush home from the office.
annotation.walkthrough: "Tear back" suggests rushing home, and even hints at reversing a word; but the back belongs to office.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ripe fruit is ready to eat, and a plan ripe for action is ready for it.

entries.clue: Scullion cleaned out a special potty in slow motion (6,4)

indicators.note: a thing cleaned out has had its insides emptied, leaving its outer letters
potty means crazy, so the letters go mad

blocks.note: the first and last letters of scullion
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A kitchen servant slowly cleaning out a special chamber pot.
annotation.walkthrough: A scullion is a kitchen drudge, and "cleaned out" and "potty" both sound like his chores until you read potty as crazy.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to move at a snail's pace is to crawl along, the slowest motion there is.

entries.clue: Touch a lip to smear oil (9)

indicators.note: a smear smudges things out of shape, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Dabbing oil onto a lip.
annotation.walkthrough: "Smear oil" reads as one action, but smear is the instruction and oil alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: patchouli is an aromatic essential oil, strongly associated with hippies.

entries.clue: Struggle to catch film titles, like Miss Saigon? (10)

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the struggle wraps round the film and titles

blocks.note: to vie is to struggle, compete; split to hold the rest
E.T., Spielberg's film
titles are names

annotation.surface: Straining to read the credits of a musical set in Vietnam.
annotation.walkthrough: Miss Saigon is a musical, but read as a beauty-contest title it is a young woman from Saigon; the question mark covers that stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a woman crowned Miss Saigon would come from that Vietnamese city.

entries.clue: Sailor and cook joining employees in corporation (7)

blocks.note: AB = able seaman
to do food is to cook it
the men are the workforce

annotation.surface: A sailor and a cook taking jobs in a big company.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes corporation a company; it is an old jokey word for a pot belly.
annotation.definitionFit: Dated slang: a corporation is a large belly, so the abdomen.

entries.clue: Attracts several taking part in apprenticeship (7)

indicators.note: what takes part in something is a part of it, so the answer is part of the next word

blocks.note: surface padding: the apprentices are several, but the word gives no letters
the inside of the word, with appr- and -hip trimmed off

annotation.surface: An apprenticeship scheme that draws in several recruits.
annotation.walkthrough: "Several" only dresses the picture of recruits signing up; the letters come from the long word alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to entice is to lure or attract.

entries.clue: Pot eventually gets everyone high (4)

indicators.note: what comes eventually comes at the end, so take the last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of pot
everyone = all

annotation.surface: Cannabis finally getting the whole party stoned.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug surface makes "high" mean stoned; it means lofty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tall building is a high one.

entries.clue: About to be affected by a loveless taunt that’s unbecoming (5,3)

indicators.note: love is O, a zero score in tennis, so something loveless has lost an O

blocks.note: IN FOR, as in "in for trouble", losing its O
the article taken as it stands
a dig is a taunt

annotation.surface: Mocking someone with a spiteful taunt is beneath you.
annotation.walkthrough: The O comes out of the first phrase, not the taunt. Infra dig is short for Latin infra dignitatem, beneath one's dignity.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin tag: something infra dig is beneath one's dignity, so unbecoming.

entries.clue: God bringing rain, and where it may go cyclically (5)

indicators.note: going round in a cycle, letters from the front come round to the back

blocks.note: rain runs down a drain

annotation.surface: A rain god, and the endless water cycle.
annotation.walkthrough: "It" points back to the rain in the definition, so the clue reads as one idea; cycling is apt, as rain goes round too.
annotation.definitionFit: Hindu myth: Indra is the Vedic god of rain and thunder.

entries.clue: Areas for discussion about large section of Life on Earth (5)

indicators.note: about means around, so the discussion areas surround the large

blocks.note: fora is the Latin plural of forum, split to hold the rest
L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: Discussion groups about a big part of a nature documentary.
annotation.walkthrough: Life on Earth is David Attenborough's TV series, which the capitals point at; here it means just life on the planet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by part: flora is plant life, one section of all life on Earth.

entries.clue: One is set on starter of avocado in runny paste (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece set on another is written after it
a word's starter is its first letter
what is in something sits inside it, so A goes into the word for runny

blocks.note: a runny liquid is thin, split to hold the rest
the first letter of avocado
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: A runny paste with avocado as a starter, like a dip.
annotation.walkthrough: The food surface runs straight into the definition, and "starter" looks like the first course rather than a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: tahini is a paste of ground sesame seeds.

entries.clue: Vessel departs, in what manner? (4)

blocks.note: d. = departs, as on a timetable
how = in what manner

annotation.surface: Someone asking how a boat is leaving.
annotation.walkthrough: D for departs is the railway timetable abbreviation, as A is for arrives.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a dhow is a lateen-sailed Arab trading vessel.

entries.clue: Substantial fare from route taken by ocean liner? (4,6)

blocks.note: the biggest dish of a meal
the main is the open sea, and a ship's route is its course

annotation.surface: Dinner on a cruise ship.
annotation.walkthrough: "The main" is an old word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; the question mark flags that fanciful reading.
annotation.definitionFit: The main course is the substantial dish of a meal, and whimsically a course over the main, the sea.

entries.clue: Flower in a hole, again at its limits like that (10)

indicators.note: a word's limits are its two ends, so keep only its first and last letters

blocks.note: the article taken as it stands
a gap is a hole
the first and last letters of again
thus = like that

annotation.surface: A flower planted in a hole, trimmed back again.
annotation.walkthrough: "In" is surface glue here, not a container instruction: the pieces simply follow one another.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: agapanthus, the African lily, is a flowering plant with blue globes of blooms.

entries.clue: Losing head, blowing motor race (4)

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, and losing it drops that letter

blocks.note: windy weather is blowing hard; minus its first letter W

annotation.surface: A car blowing its engine and losing its lead in a race.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blowing" looks like an engine failing, but it describes the weather.
annotation.definitionFit: An American abbreviation: the Indy is the Indianapolis 500, the famous motor race.
